basis: CAMS1 comprises AVMs in the medial forebrain and nasal territory; these defining sites map to vascular, neurologic and pulmonary axes.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: nasal AVMs are part of the defining medial prosencephalic territory of CAMS1; the nose belongs to this axis.

basis: Developmental delay/ID 5/5; camptodactyly 2/5 supports skeletal involvement. Otitis is a secondary diagnosis; hearing impairment only 1/5.

decisions.otologic: none: recurrent/chronic otitis (80-99%) is a separate secondary disease; intrinsic hearing impairment is reported in only 1/5.

basis: Skeletal, hearing and palatal defects define the named triad; cleft palate 18/18. Intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%, retained as involved under the three-primary cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: palatal defects define the named syndrome; cleft palate occurs in 18/18 and tooth agenesis in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%; the three primary slots retain the defining skeletal, ear and palatal triad.

basis: Myopathy 8/8 with neuropathic/CNS disease; sensorineural hearing loss 3/3. Hepatic failure and cataract each have single-patient evidence without established cohort frequency.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic failure in one assessed patient (1/1) does not establish >=30% prevalence across the eight-patient myopathy cohort.

basis: Inborn sulfide oxidation defect with lactic acidosis; encephalopathy 3/3 and coma 2/3 establish neurologic injury. Elevated CK alone does not establish myopathy.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy occurs in 3/3 and coma in 2/3; these are organ manifestations of the defining metabolic enzyme deficiency.

basis: Susceptibility-only concept; neither manifest marrow disease nor MIRAGE organ abnormalities are established. Future myeloid neoplasm risk does not establish organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: the definition specifies inherited susceptibility, not manifest marrow disease; myelodysplasia/leukemia is a later risk.

basis: Liver injury 21/21, cleft palate 25/32, cardiomyopathy 8/21; coagulation abnormalities 40-50% omitted at cap. CK alone insufficient; rhabdomyolysis 23%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate in 25/32 (78%) is a direct congenital oral defect and merits retention under the four-axis cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: CK elevation 19/32 alone does not establish myopathy; rhabdomyolysis 7/30 (23%) is below threshold; other organs take priority at cap.

basis: Dermal, limb and eye malformations define syndrome; dental defects 30-79%. Neurologic features (ID 30-79%, microcephaly 80-99%) omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: microphthalmia and ocular colobomas (30-79%) are characteristic malformations in the defining skin-limb-eye syndrome.

basis: Lethal OI-spectrum bone fragility; pulmonary hypoplasia directly impairs lung function and contributes to respiratory failure in most perinatally lethal cases.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is common in perinatally lethal OI (>30%); structural lung underdevelopment qualifies beyond mechanical chest restriction.

basis: Mitochondrial disorder; cardiomyopathy 4/4, ophthalmoplegia/ptosis 2/4. Exercise intolerance alone cannot establish muscle damage; renal, hepatic and hearing findings each 1/4.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: exercise intolerance 2/4 can reflect cardiomyopathy; myopathy has no frequency, and CK elevation occurs in only 1/4.
